reuse.why: Introduces a shared NO_TEMPLATE_SQL fragment but no shared category selection; setZero gets a fourth hand-written copy of the average actions' category query instead of all actions sharing one.

duplication.why: The template condition is factored into a constant for the SQL sites, but it is defined a second time as hasSavedTemplates in JS with the same literal list, and the hidden/group-hidden filter remains copied across four queries plus a JS branch.

placement.why: Everything stays in budget/actions.ts where the actions live, but the eligibility rule is split between an SQL fragment, a JS predicate and per-query WHERE clauses.

scope.why: Only category eligibility for the month-wide actions changes.

maintainability.why: Better than inlining the template rule everywhere, but the SQL and JS versions of 'has templates' must be kept in sync by hand and the hidden rule still lives in five places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The tree has no shared month-wide category selection to go around.

disguised_duplication.where: The saved-template rule is expressed twice in different forms: NO_TEMPLATE_SQL (SQL IN list) and hasSavedTemplates (JS includes on the same list); setZero's new query re-copies the average actions' query.

one_place.where: The template part is split between NO_TEMPLATE_SQL (setZero, set3/6/12MonthAvg) and hasSavedTemplates (copyPreviousMonth), and the hidden/group-hidden part is still written separately in each query and in copyPreviousMonth's JS check.
